AHA-7.2-R1.section: 7.2 Diuretics and Decongestion Strategies in Patients With HF
AHA-7.2-R1.text: In patients with HF who have fluid retention, diuretics are recommended to relieve congestion, improve symptoms, and prevent worsening HF.

AHA-7.2-SYN.text: Loop diuretics are the preferred diuretic agents for use in most patients with HF. [...] The treatment goal of diuretic use is to eliminate clinical evidence of fluid retention, using the lowest dose possible to maintain euvolemia. [...] diuretics should not be used in isolation but always combined with other GDMT for HF that reduces hospitalizations and prolongs survival.

AHA-7.2-TEXT1.text: In outpatients with HF, diuretic therapy is commonly initiated with low doses, and the dose is increased until urine output increases and weight decreases, generally by 0.5 to 1.0 kg daily.

AHA-9.3-R2.section: 9.3 Diuretics in Hospitalized Patients: Decongestion Strategy
AHA-9.3-R2.text: For patients hospitalized with HF, therapy with diuretics and other guideline-directed medications should be titrated with a goal to resolve clinical evidence of congestion to reduce symptoms and rehospitalizations.

AHA-9.3-R3.section: 9.3 Diuretics in Hospitalized Patients: Decongestion Strategy
AHA-9.3-R3.text: For patients requiring diuretic treatment during hospitalization for HF, the discharge regimen should include a plan for adjustment of diuretics to decrease rehospitalizations.

AHA-9.3-TEXT2.text: Monitoring HF treatment includes careful measurement of fluid intake and output, vital signs, standing body weight at the same time each day, and clinical signs and symptoms of congestion and hypoperfusion. Daily laboratory tests during active medication adjustment include serum electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine concentrations.

CSI-FIG7.section: Fig. 7. Treatment outline for heart failure profiles
CSI-FIG7.text: CONGESTION AT REST? NO (PCWP<18 mmHg) / YES (PCWP>18 mmHg). LOW PERFUSION AT REST? NO (CI > 2.2 L/min/m2) / YES (CI < 2.2 L/min/m2). No congestion + no low perfusion: GDMT. No congestion + low perfusion: INOTROPES +/- IV FLUIDS. Congestion + no low perfusion: DIURETICS, VASODILATORS. Congestion + low perfusion: DIURETICS, INOTROPES.

CSI-2.2-DIUR.text: Current guidelines recommend intravenously administered diuretics as first line therapy for volume overload. Loop diuretics are initial diuretics of choice.

CSI-2.4.1-HFPEF.text: Relieve congestion with diuretics Judicious use of loop diuretic with careful monitoring of renal function

AHA-9.1-R1.section: 9.1 Assessment of Patients Hospitalized With Decompensated HF
AHA-9.1-R1.text: In patients hospitalized with HF, severity of congestion and adequacy of perfusion should be assessed to guide triage and initial therapy.

AHA-T23.text: 1. SBP <90 mm Hg or mean BP <60 mm Hg. 2. Cardiac index <2.2 L/min/m2. 3. Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure >15 mm Hg. [...] *Diagnosis of shock requires ≥1 criteria to be present along with cardiac index <2.0 L/min/m2 and SBP <90 mm Hg.

AHA-9.5-SHOCKTEXT.section: 9.5 Evaluation and Management of Cardiogenic Shock, Synopsis
AHA-9.5-SHOCKTEXT.text: Hypotension (eg, SBP <90 mm Hg) is the primary clinical manifestation of shock but is not sufficient for the diagnosis. Additionally, end-organ hypoperfusion should be present as a consequence of cardiac dysfunction (Tables 22, 23, 24).

CSI-2.2.3-VASO.text: Vasodilators should be avoided in patients with reduced filling pressures or symptomatic hypotension. [...] Nitroglycerin exhibits primarily venodilation at low doses and mild arterial vasodilation at higher doses; thus, it is the preferred agent for preload reduction. [...] The primary disadvantages of nitroprusside are hypotension, tachyphylaxis and risk of cyanide and thiocyanate accumulation. In patients with substantial hepatic or renal impairment, this agent should be avoided or dose and duration of therapy should be minimized.

AHA-7.2-R2.section: 7.2 Diuretics and Decongestion Strategies in Patients With HF
AHA-7.2-R2.text: For patients with HF and congestive symptoms, addition of a thiazide (eg, metolazone) to treatment with a loop diuretic should be reserved for patients who do not respond to moderate- or high-dose loop diuretics to minimize electrolyte abnormalities.

AHA-9.3-R4.section: 9.3 Diuretics in Hospitalized Patients: Decongestion Strategy
AHA-9.3-R4.text: In patients hospitalized with HF when diuresis is inadequate to relieve symptoms and signs of congestion, it is reasonable to intensify the diuretic regimen using either: a. higher doses of intravenous loop diuretics; or b. addition of a second diuretic.

limitations: The congestion input is an ESTIMATE from the chest patch, not a measurement; only the middle of its range is reliable (journey R7).
Cardiac index and blood pressure are measured values from the record, never estimated.
The dataset has no medication list: the current diuretic is 'unknown' unless a simulated input is shown and labelled.
The tool never suggests a dose. Dose tables are kept out of the AI input.

The low-blood-flow / low-blood-pressure review is decided by code alone from measured values and cited cut-offs; that it always leads to a clinician review is a safety choice of the team, not a guideline sentence.
The 31 test cases were written from the guidelines by the engineering team and have not been reviewed by a clinician.
A decision-support gate that abstains is working as designed; most of this cohort has low measured perfusion or a middle-zone congestion estimate.
_meta.disclaimer: Decision support for the clinician. The clinician decides; no dose is suggested.
